answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying each account's weight to verified history, not to the number of accounts. A newcomer stands on an open dune: nothing is granted, and it must make one honest contribution at a time, attested by established peers, before earning any standing. Reputation builds slowly, like a sparrow gathering nesting material branch by branch, and a gale of freshly minted keys cannot carry that weight away. A farm spinning up thousands of identities gets thousands of empty shells, none able to vote or earn, since influence flows only from durable, witnessed work.
